newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mexico scraps tariff on Australian wool.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mexico scraps tariff on Australian wool.

text.p: Mexico has agreed to scrap its 15 percent tariff on Australian wool imports, Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Wednesday.

"We have secured a lowering of the Mexican tariff against Australian wool products -- processed and partly processed and raw -- from 15 percent to zero percent," Fischer told a business breakfast. The tariff would begin to come down next year, and would open up "another pipeline" for Australian wool exports into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), Fischer said.
NAFTA comprises Canada, the United States and Mexico.
The bilateral deal was negotiated during the recent World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore.
"I guess there was self-interest by them ... to provide another conduit into the U.S. market to compete with the China pipeline into the U.S. market," he said.
Fischer said the benefit to Australian wool exports would be slow to materialise due to the size of Mexico's milling industry, but he stressed the move was important strategic step.
"That particular lowering of tariffs is of very great benefit to Australia and will be increasingly so," he said.
